parsed.study_design: Quasi-experimental difference-in-differences study using matched census-tract controls
parsed.population_and_sample: Households in low-income settlements in Recife, represented by temporally harmonized census tracts from the 1991, 2000, and 2010 Brazilian censuses; the baseline analysis included 19 ZEIS-treated and 54 propensity-score-matched untreated census tracts.
parsed.exposure: Implementation of Social Interest Special Zones (ZEIS), a municipal land-use zoning and regularization policy for low-income settlements.
parsed.outcome: Census-tract percentages of households accessing piped water through the public network and sewage services through the general network; additional outcomes were homeownership, bathrooms per household, and garbage collection access.
parsed.rationale: The study directly estimates how a municipal legal and urban-governance intervention affected household water and sewage-network access in low-income areas. Sections 3.1–3.2 (pp. 10–19) identify the population, ZEIS exposure, census-derived outcomes, matched comparison group, and difference-in-differences design; Tables 2–3 and Section 4 (pp. 20–23) report positive estimated effects on public water- and sewage-network access.
